data.command: [REDACTED:path] -m ddflow --agent=merge-done review fix-B-complete-self-approves-over-person-only-partial --gate rubber_duck,critic --intent 'Refute this change: `ddflow complete` now REFUSES (instead of silently auto-forcing) over a measured baseline-red partial that only a person may accept; the date-shared predicate is gate_accept.person_only, used by both _only_unavailable and the complete_unavailable rule. Find the input where this wrongly blocks a completion the operator already accepted, or where a forced completion still slips through unreported. If uncertain, report nothing.'

ci_scope.why: 42 test file(s) its change reaches, 23 always-run guard file(s); the selected tests failed; the always-run guards failed

chunk_findings.detail:
The new policy.py guard filters the person-only gate out of the `target` set that is then used to decide the `complete_unavailable` predicate. That is not a refusal; it treats the person-only partial as if it were absent. Concretely, with two unmet required gates:

- `g1` is an ordinary `unavailable` coverage gap (`g1 in coverage_gaps`, `GA.person_only(it, g1)` is `False`).
- `g2` is a measured baseline-red partial with `baseline.red is True` and no `baseline.auto.accepted` (`GA.person_only(it, g2)` is `True`), and `g2` is not a coverage gap.

The failed-outcome loop does not reject this completion. In the set comprehension, `g2` is removed by the new `and not GA.person_only(it, g)` condition, leaving `target = {g1}`. Since the function’s existing decision is `target <= set(it.coverage_gaps)`, this returns `True`, so the `complete_unavailable` rule still answers the completion over the person-only partial. The approval site guard does an `any(...)` check and would refuse, but the rule’s own predicate does not; this is exactly the “forced completion still slips through unreported” case the change claims to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py `and not GA.person_only(it, g)`

chunk_findings.detail: The new `person_only` guard is keyed on the original automatic gate-run evidence (`evidence.baseline.auto.accepted` is `False`), and the added tests only model that unapproved state. The operator-accepted path is never exercised: `_person_only_baseline_red` creates the `gate.partial` record with `baseline.auto.accepted: False`, and none of the three new tests makes the `ddflow approve T1 unit_tests` call the refusal message itself says is required. In that state, the operator's acceptance is recorded outside the `auto.accepted` field, so `person_only()` still returns `True`; `_only_unavailable()` then returns `False`, and `ddflow complete T1` wrongly exits with code 3 instead of completing an already accepted completion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:person_only

chunk_findings.detail: The test promises both sites share `gate_accept.person_only` and cannot drift, but it never calls that helper and never asserts the complementary case. Given a `complete_unavailable.when` that returns False for every `partial` (or False because some other gate is unmet), the only assertion (`when(...) is False` on a baseline-red item) still passes, so a completion site that does not read `person_only` stays green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_policy.py:test_complete_unavailable_predicate_and_site_share_the_person_only_guard

chunk_findings.detail: The suite never builds the two inputs this change is supposed to distinguish. An item whose measured partial still has `baseline.auto.accepted` False but that a person has already accepted with `ddflow approve` is not completed in any test, so a guard that keeps refusing after that accept is not caught. A forced completion (`complete` with an explicit approval that should be allowed, or that should be reported if it still spends the standing rule) is also absent, so a force that still slips through unreported leaves every new assertion green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_policy.py:test_a_routine_completion_never_auto_answers_a_person_only_baseline_red_partial
